events.content:
The welcome page is now a server component that logs each page view using Next.js's after from next/server, which runs the logging only after the response has been sent. I checked this against the after docs bundled with the installed Next.js (16.4.0-canary.52). next build passes, and with next start two requests logged two page views.

Files:
- app/page.tsx: an async server component that shows the welcome message. It calls await connection() so the page is rendered on every request, then uses after(...) to call logPageView({ path, timestamp }).
- lib/analytics.ts: logPageView sends a page_view event to the ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT environment variable. If that variable isn't set, it just prints the event to the console. It catches all errors, so a failed analytics call never affects the user.

Why connection() is needed: my first build without it made the page static. after then ran only once at build time (the log line appeared during "Generating static pages"), not on each visit. With connection() the route builds as dynamic (ƒ /), so every visit is logged.

Limitation: in pages and layouts you can't call cookies() or headers() inside the after callback. If you want request data in the event, read it during render and pass it into the callback.

Other changes: the build added .next/ and next-env.d.ts, and edited tsconfig.json itself (it set jsx to react-jsx and added .next/dev/types//.ts to include). The changes to package.json and package-lock.json were already there before I started, and I left them alone.
